citation: Resendez, M., & Azin, M. (2012). A study on the effects of Houghton Mifflin Harcourt's Journeys program: Year 1 final report. Jackson, WY: PRES Associates, Inc. (Planning, Research & Evaluation Services).
report_number: PRES Associates, Inc. (independent evaluation); HMH Journeys RCT Year 1 Final Report, August 2012
design: Cluster RCT; random assignment at the TEACHER/CLASS level WITHIN schools (NOT school-level, contra the registry's 'School' tag). 6 elementary schools (AZ, RI, DC, LA), 44 teachers/classes randomized (23 Journeys treatment, 21 control), final analytic sample 1046 students retained through Year 1 (541 treatment, 505 control). Intervention = Houghton Mifflin Harcourt 'Journeys' (2012) comprehensive K-6 reading/language arts core curriculum plus the accompanying HMH professional development/training (5-6 hr initial + half-day follow-up) vs business-as-usual (six distinct existing reading/language arts programs the schools already used). Subject = reading/literacy/language arts; grades K-2 (2011-12 = Year 1 of a 2-year study that followed students into grades 1-3 in 2012-13). Outcomes = ITBS (Iowa Tests of Basic Skills) Form C norm-referenced subtests. Analysis = three-level HLM (time within student within teacher) with Group covariate; teacher level of analysis matches the unit of random assignment, so impact estimates account for clustering.
problems: ASSIGNMENT-LEVEL DISCREPANCY: the registry tags row 98 as 'School'-level assignment, but the report unambiguously states random assignment occurred at the TEACHER level within schools (pp.13-14, 'random assignment of teachers to a treatment ... within schools'; Table A15 df=911 at slope level; 44 teachers/classes are the clusters). I recorded the report's actual design (teacher/class-randomized, cluster_adjusted=true). This is the SAME PRES-Associates evaluation team as the 2009 enVisionMATH study (row 97), but a DISTINCT study (different program: Journeys reading vs enVisionMATH math; different sample). | The report's headline 'Effect Size' (Table A15, p.98) is explicitly defined (Appendix B, p.103) as 'Hedges's g for intervention effects estimated from HLM analyses' = HLM impact coefficient gamma divided by the unadjusted pooled within-group posttest SD, g = gamma / sqrt[((n1-1)S1^2+(n2-1)S2^2)/(n1+n2-2)]. This is exactly the spec's preferred model-based-impact / standardizing-SD approach. The report's formula OMITS the small-sample J correction (so its reported numbers are technically Cohen's d / WWC-style SMD); I applied J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 (J ~ 0.999, negligible). My recomputed g matches the report's reported ES to 2 decimals on every significant outcome (Reading Comp 0.20, Vocabulary 0.15, Spelling 0.15, Reading Words 0.39), confirming I used the correct standardizing SDs/Ns (Table A14, p.96). | ICC: the report never reports the actual design-effect ICC (only discusses an assumed range 0.07-0.55 / WWC default 0.20 for power calcs); per spec I left icc=null rather than guess. | n_clusters=44 (teachers/classes), nested in 6 schools. | Word Analysis (K-2) and Language (1-2) program effects were non-significant; the report left their ES cells blank in Table A15, but I computed and recorded their g (0.07 and 0.02) from the reported coefficient and posttest SDs. | Pretest non-equivalence on Word Analysis only (treatment higher, p=.005, Table A1/Table 5); the report controlled for it (the 3-level model adjusts for the Group covariate and baseline level), and a 2-level pretest-controlled model gave consistent results. | All extracted contrasts are immediate end-of-Year-1 post (Spring 2012); the 2-year endpoint (Spring 2013) is a separate publication (Resendez & Azin 2013, Year 2 Final Report) downloaded for cross-check at data/fulltext/resendez_azin_2013_year2.pdf but NOT extracted here, since row 98 = the 2012 Year 1 report and the meta-analysis treats the short-duration Year-1 wave. | Original HMH-hosted PDF URL now returns 503; obtained the identical file via the Wayback Machine (archived 2024-07-08, HTTP 200, 5.3 MB).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Journeys reading/language-arts curriculum + HMH teacher PD/training vs business-as-usual (existing reading programs)
effect_sizes.test_name: ITBS (Iowa Tests of Basic Skills) Form C - Reading Comprehension subtest scale score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (Spring 2012, end of Year 1 of 2-year study)
effect_sizes.g_method: Model-based: g = J * (gamma / s_pooled). gamma = HLM 'Slope Year 1' program-effect coefficient = 3.87 (Table A15, p.98), SE = 0.97. s_pooled = sqrt[((n_t-1)*sd_t^2+(n_c-1)*sd_c^2)/(n_t+n_c-2)] from Table A14 posttest SDs/Ns = sqrt[((498*20.15^2)+(478*18.75^2))/976] = 19.477. d = 3.87/19.477 = 0.1987. df = n_t+n_c-2 = 976, J = 1-3/(4*976-1) = 0.99923, g = 0.1985. g_se = J*(SE/s_pooled) = 0.99923*(0.97/19.477) = 0.0498; g_var = 0.002476. Matches report's reported ES = 0.20 (report's 'Hedges's g' formula, Appendix B p.103, omits J).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table A15 p.98 (coefficient/SE/ES); Table A14 p.96 (posttest M/SD/N); Figure 54 p.47
effect_sizes.notes: Statistically significant (p=.001) favoring Journeys. Lead reading outcome (also used to define student ability subgroups). 3-level HLM (time/student/teacher) with Group covariate; teacher level matches randomization unit so SE is cluster-adjusted. K-2 combined.
